intro: Suggestions to improve the site and the decision process. NONE of these has been implemented. Review each option, then choose a path. Options are listed with the trade-off.

items.title: Add the remaining Strip properties
options: A) Add MGM / Mandalay Bay, Caesars properties and Resorts World next (official poker pages and structure sheets).
B) Add only the properties with 2+ single-entry events in the next two weeks.
C) Keep the scope at Venetian and Wynn.
items.tradeoff: A gives the broadest view but takes the most research time. B is faster. C is the cheapest and fully verified now.

items.title: Automate structure-sheet classification
options: A) Script that reads each official structure PDF and flags re-entry, rebuy, add-on and flight words automatically.
B) Keep manual review with a checklist per row.
C) Manual review plus a second reviewer.
items.tradeoff: A scales and is consistent but can miss unusual wording. B is accurate but slow. C adds confidence at the cost of time.
items.status: Implemented, with the scope kept honest
items.implemented_as: The classification is now mechanical where the document is explicit and manual only where wording is ambiguous. scripts/build_structure_registry.py holds the reading of all 37 sheets; scripts/audit.py re-derives every Venetian row's fee, chips, late-registration wording, clock close and guarantee against the sheet it cites and fails the build on any mismatch. Automatic keyword hunting for 're-entry' was not used as the decision rule: all 24 silent sheets contain no such word, and treating that as 'single entry' would be an inference. Silence is labelled silence.

items.title: Capture dated snapshots of every official source
options: A) Save a PDF or HTML copy of each official source with the date checked.
B) Save links only (current approach).
C) Snapshot only the sources behind single-entry rows.
items.tradeoff: A and C protect against changes; B is simplest but links can change silently.

items.title: Add a nightly-rate capture step
options: A) Record an official nightly rate for each hotel on the chosen dates, with the date and tax shown.
B) Ask the user for a quoted rate.
C) Show resort fees only (current state).
items.tradeoff: A gives a true cost figure but needs travel dates. B depends on the user. C is what is verified now.

items.title: Choose a quality measure for hotels
options: A) AAA Diamond rating (official AAA listing).
B) Forbes Travel Guide star rating.
C) The user's own criteria (for example room size, reviews).
items.tradeoff: A and B are third-party rating bodies with official listings. C is personal and needs the user to define it.

items.title: Walking-time method
options: A) Use a map routing service and record the date checked.
B) Use each resort's own map or concierge.
C) Estimate from straight-line distance (not recommended; cannot be verified).
items.tradeoff: A and B are verifiable; C is an estimate and conflicts with the 'never infer' rule.
items.recommendation: Option A, and it is what the site now does
items.implemented_as: Google Maps walking directions were read 2026-11-17 for eight hotels' trips to The Venetian Poker Room, and every figure was checked against a second, independent router: the OSRM foot-profile matrix built 2026-11-16 from geocoded official addresses. The two agree on the 30-minute verdict for every pair they share. The Wynn side is covered by the OSRM matrix alone and is labelled 'single router'. Each row states the date read, the router count and a live route link, so any figure can be re-checked by hand.

items.title: Add interactive filters
options: A) Filters by date, buy-in cap, guarantee minimum and property (JavaScript on the table pages).
B) Keep static tables sorted by value.
C) Add a day planner that builds an 8 AM–close schedule from verified start times.
items.tradeoff: A and C add real decision value. B is what is built now.
items.implemented_as: Search boxes, date filters and category filters run on every table, and a day planner now picks one primary event per day with a fallback, using published start times and printed registration cut-offs. Buy-in-cap and guarantee-minimum filters are not built yet.

items.title: Monitor for changes
options: A) Scheduled job that re-fetches each official page weekly and flags changed rows.
B) Manual re-check before each trip.
C) No automation.
items.tradeoff: A keeps data current but needs hosting; B is cheap; C risks stale data.
items.recommendation: Option A, already wired — it just needs a first baseline
items.implemented_as: Three workflows exist (recheck.yml, source-monitor.yml, plan-refresh.yml) and 82 official URLs are in data/source_monitor.json, but no hash baseline has been taken yet, so nothing can be diffed. The next run of source-monitor.yml establishes the baseline; until then the monitor page shows 82 URLs as 'never checked'.

items.title: Name the single-entry standard in one place
options: A) Keep the current definition (no re-entry, rebuy or add-on stated in the official structure sheet).
B) Require poker-room confirmation for every row before it counts as single-entry.
C) Use both: sheet-based by default, confirmation for events the user will play.
items.tradeoff: A is clear but depends on documents; B is strongest but slow; C balances both.
items.status: Implementing — the wording was already changed to match
items.implemented_as: Every Venetian one-day row reads 'sheet silent on re-entry' and the 45 of them sit in their own category, never in the single-entry group. The structure-sheet register states the standard in one place, and Q01 and Q09 record that a poker-room answer is still needed before any row is called single-entry.

items.title: Fix the repo setup
options: A) Keep Pages on main, path '/' (current; site files are at the root).
B) Move the site into /docs and switch Pages to /docs.
C) Use a GitHub Actions build (needs a workflow file).
items.tradeoff: A is in place now. B keeps the root clean. C allows a build step but adds a workflow.
